title: The Base and the Arm as One: A Jacobian With Eight Columns, a Weight on Moving the Base, and a Line Drawn Farther Than the Arm Alone Can Reach

artifact.note: moving a hand with the base and the arm together: a Jacobian of eight columns (the base's forward speed and turning rate, then the six joints) giving the hand's velocity in the world, the rates that give the hand a wanted velocity at least cost (a weighted damped least squares with a price on moving the base), and a simulated line drawn by the hand a metre and a half long, with the base only turning and driving along its heading, to compare with the arm alone
